title: Three Temperatures
memory_text: Three chambers appeared identical from the corridor. The first inhabitant was restless, the second quiet, and the third scarcely moved. I had begun a theory of character before Clara asked where the cold draught entered. Lenz held a strip of paper by the window; it shivered without our touching it. I rearranged the chambers and obtained a new order of restlessness. The paper rustled all afternoon, an insufferably accurate witness. I repeated the measurements before entering anyone's intentions in my ledger. The change did not make the inhabitants less individual. It merely obliged me to stop naming a private motive where I had measured a room badly.
prior_expectations: Comparable looking chambers would have comparable conditions
observations: A draft altered responses when chamber positions changed
decisions: I repeated the trial and marked the cold wall
consequences: Environmental checks preceded character attribution
belief_changes: Appearance does not establish environmental equivalence
relationship_changes: Clara and Lenz earned the right to contest my interpretation
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: Two Measures of Applause
memory_text: The Archbishop behaved ceremoniously whenever no one desired a performance. I put a little bell beside his platform and asked Clara to wait behind a partition. At its sound he remained seated. At Clara's cough he crossed the ledge. I rang the bell again with more authority than the instrument deserved. He turned away. I had expected a correspondence between sound and movement. Instead I discovered that a sound from a familiar person may belong to quite another category than an equally loud bell. Clara's cough persisted into supper, and I found myself listening for it. I called the trial inconclusive, gave the Archbishop a more sheltered ledge, and stopped ringing the bell for guests.
prior_expectations: The bell should reliably summon the Archbishop
observations: He approached at Clara's voice but not the bell
decisions: I ended public bell demonstrations
consequences: Clara's familiar sound became an alternative cue
belief_changes: Loudness alone did not explain the observed choice
relationship_changes: Clara's ordinary presence proved experimentally relevant
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: Salt in the Cracked Bowl
memory_text: Lenz brought me a bowl which could no longer hold the instrument-room rinse water. Rosa thought it perfectly serviceable for bread. I objected that a scientific household ought not live among broken things. At supper the soup tasted so heavily of salt that I put down my spoon. Rosa swore she had used no more than usual; I had neglected to eat since morning. The fissure in the bowl held a dark line of broth. Later I kept screws in it, despite my earlier lecture on standards. A failed object may be perfectly competent at another task. I said this once, and Rosa asked whether I intended to charge admission for the discovery.
prior_expectations: A cracked laboratory vessel was useless
observations: The vessel served other purposes; hunger altered my perception of supper
decisions: I retained it for dry tools
consequences: The cracked bowl became a recurring household object
belief_changes: Failure depends on the task assigned to an object
relationship_changes: Rosa and Lenz practiced repair and reuse without apology
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Crooked Pair
memory_text: Two new forms came from similar vessels. One possessed the handsome symmetry I had worked to achieve; the other bore a crooked shoulder and an inconvenient appetite. When offered a passage to their food, the handsome one soon rested against the glass. Its counterpart found a route beneath the paper screen and returned to eat. Marta wrote the discrepancy without ornament. I redesigned the screen three times, each version prettier and less useful. Lenz moved one fold with a pencil, and the awkward creature accepted the resulting shelter. The well-proportioned one did not recover at once, nor did the other become beautiful. Both remained alive for observation, though my first catalogue had implied that only one deserved a future.
prior_expectations: Fine proportion would correlate with better function
observations: The awkward figure navigated and ate more effectively
decisions: I retained both subjects and changed the shelter
consequences: Later notes distinguished appearance from function
belief_changes: Aesthetic selection had hidden a practical weakness
relationship_changes: Marta and Lenz documented capabilities I undervalued
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Bearing's Unwelcome Voice
memory_text: A repaired balance emitted a faint scrape on every turn. The readings appeared sound, but the noise lodged behind my teeth. Lenz asked whether the bearing needed replacing. I demanded a blind test and made six judgments about when the wheel was moving. I was correct twice. The offending sound came from a loose cover rather than the measured wheel. I had spent the morning listening to an apparatus I supposed I understood better than my own assumptions. We fixed the cover and began hiding the machine's operating state in selected trials. I still disliked the scrape, which is no refutation of its insignificance. Lenz pointed out that my strongest estimate had been the least accurate. I did not congratulate him.
prior_expectations: An intrusive sound meant the readings were compromised
observations: Blinded estimates failed and the cover produced the scrape
decisions: I repaired the cover and introduced hidden runs
consequences: Sound was separated from inferred apparatus performance
belief_changes: Discomfort is not a measurement
relationship_changes: Lenz gained more control over trial design
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Empty Control Vessel
memory_text: A preserved sample clouded its glass twice. Marta suspected the vessel rather than anything living. We placed an empty control beside it. The empty glass clouded as well. Our result withdrew an attractive answer without providing a replacement. The room smelled of old cork and damp wood. Clara traced the dampness to a leaking sill, which I had ignored because it made the northern light picturesque. We moved the rack and repeated the observations over several weeks. I was tempted to declare the control contaminated merely to regain my earlier theory. Instead I wrote unresolved across the page. Later visitors praised our photographs of clouded glass for their mysterious depth. I refrained from describing that effect as a discovery.
prior_expectations: Clouding indicated a change within the specimen
observations: An empty vessel also clouded and the sill was wet
decisions: I moved the rack and retained an unresolved control
consequences: An attractive observation remained experimentally ambiguous
belief_changes: No preferred cause can be granted the status of evidence
relationship_changes: Marta and Clara constrained an erroneous conclusion
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: Beyond the Curtain
memory_text: I had learned to close the linen curtain in hot weather, but had not ceased resenting the view it concealed. One afternoon I heard a light tapping beyond it and thought the Queen was summoning me. Clara heard it too. We waited for a repetition and found that a loose ring on the cord struck the frame. The Queen remained behind her shelter, declining the attention with which I had planned to reward her. We secured the ring. Thereafter I noticed myself anticipating a sound that would never return. The curtain carried the faint smell of starch in the evening heat. It was no magnificent discovery, merely proof that my desire to be called might supply half the summons.
prior_expectations: The Queen's tapping was deliberate
observations: A curtain ring rather than the Queen produced the sound
decisions: I fixed the ring and retained the curtain
consequences: Expectancy persisted after its external cause was removed
belief_changes: Wanting recognition can bias interpretation of noise
relationship_changes: Clara confirmed the sound but not my initial story
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: Three Breakfasts
memory_text: I kept a record of the hour at which a difficult calculation first became intelligible. On one morning I drank coffee; on another, weak tea; on a third I neglected breakfast entirely. I achieved the answer after a long walk and proposed a doctrine concerning the virtues of hunger. Marta asked how many wrong solutions had preceded it. Twelve, against six on either other morning. My hands had shaken as I drew the final diagram. She put bread beside my book without ceremony. The dry crust tasted remarkably pleasant. I began recording errors and meals together. I still remembered the triumph first and the twelve mistakes afterward, an order of recollection convenient enough to make me suspicious.
prior_expectations: Hunger might sharpen my calculations
observations: A hungry success followed many more errors and tremor
decisions: I added meals and error counts to the ledger
consequences: Exhausted triumph was no longer treated as efficiency
belief_changes: Outcome success cannot certify its preceding method
relationship_changes: Marta challenged my selective accounting
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: A Room Without a Medium
memory_text: The hostess of the second sitting had departed. Her velvet cushions were stacked for the next tenants, but the scent of rosewater survived beneath fresh soap. My stomach tightened before anyone spoke. Marta reminded me that we had returned only for a receipt. The landlord demonstrated the newly repaired shutter; its iron catch made no noise. We took the receipt and left. I resented how swiftly a room without ritual could restore my apprehension. Recognition of a place did not establish that any spirit had visited it, yet neither did the absence of a medium erase the event of my own fear. I wrote this distinction down before the familiar room could regain its former theatricality in recollection.
prior_expectations: The absence of the sitting would remove my apprehension
observations: The room's ordinary smell evoked the former bodily state
decisions: I conducted the errand without another seance
consequences: Rosewater became shared by opposed interpretations
belief_changes: Familiarity is not independent proof of supernatural cause
relationship_changes: Marta retained the practical purpose of the visit
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Queen's Folded Paper
memory_text: The Queen arranged torn scraps into a crooked shelter. I replaced them with a handsome folded chamber decorated along the rim. She inspected it and returned to the scraps. Marta suggested leaving both. By evening the new chamber was untouched. I could not tell whether the choice reflected familiar material, the smell of paste, or the opportunity to arrange a place for herself. I wished to describe my intervention as generosity. Marta asked whom the gift had chiefly pleased. I kept both shelters available for a month. When a visitor admired my paper architecture, I accepted the compliment before remembering which part of the room the Queen had actually made.
prior_expectations: An improved shelter would be preferred
observations: The Queen returned to her own arrangement
decisions: I left both shelters available
consequences: Her stable choice had no proven single explanation
belief_changes: Offering options is not permission to control the result
relationship_changes: Marta distinguished the creature's conduct from my authorship
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Tempo of an Absent Hand
memory_text: The Ballerina moved before the first note on several occasions. I was delighted by the prospect of musical anticipation. Clara watched my arm instead and asked me to prepare the instrument out of sight. The movement came later and less regularly. I could hear the faint scrape of my sleeve whenever I reached for the crank. We repeated the trial without music, with the opening delayed, and with the sleeve restrained. Each produced some movement and some silence. I found the lack of a grand explanation intolerably ordinary. At supper I caught myself tapping the old rhythm on a glass; Clara began counting ahead of me. I stopped.
prior_expectations: Only the music cued an anticipatory movement
observations: Preparatory handling noises were possible competing cues
decisions: I varied setup and delayed interpretation
consequences: The handling sequence entered the experimental records
belief_changes: Anticipation may be learned from surrounding procedure
relationship_changes: Clara challenged performance-based explanations
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: An Empty Place in the Dream
memory_text: The glass door returned in sleep, but the Queen was absent. A table waited on the other side, laid for supper. I could smell hot bread and damp wool, though the actual bedroom had a cold hearth. I opened the dream door and found myself holding a ticket without a destination. I woke with a dry mouth and a desperate desire to check the western chamber. The Queen rested behind her shelter. Clara said I had spoken in sleep, but could repeat none of it. By breakfast my account included a ringing bell which had not appeared in my waking notes. I left the bell in pencil, where uncertainties are less apt to masquerade as facts.
prior_expectations: The dream would repeat its familiar cast
observations: Food and travel images displaced the Queen
decisions: I separated waking observation from revised dream recollection
consequences: The bell became a disputed later addition
belief_changes: Urgency on waking does not imply external danger
relationship_changes: Clara's partial report remained independent
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: Water from the Roof
memory_text: Melting snow ran through the plaster above the landing. I stood in stocking feet holding a bucket while drops struck its bottom with an extraordinarily regular note. Rosa brought another and asked why I was counting rather than moving papers. I called it an estimate of the rate of loss. She said the roof was losing and the floor was winning. My toes were numb against the stone. Clara sent me for boots and rescued the blue ledger. We saved the records but lost a pile of decorative mounts. For years the smell of damp lime recalled either expense or Rosa's laughter, depending upon which I had last endured. Both recollections were true, and neither repaired the roof.
prior_expectations: A minor thaw would spare the archive
observations: The leak threatened documents while I counted drops
decisions: I moved the records and repaired the roof
consequences: Damp lime became linked to loss and company
belief_changes: Observation without timely action can become evasion
relationship_changes: Rosa and Clara redirected attention to preservation
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: A Trial Without Spectators
memory_text: Anna agreed to inspect the proposed larger chamber on condition that I invite no admirers. I consented, chiefly because I had no admirers presently available. We assembled a paper model and weighted surrogates, not living subjects. The largest part would not pass the final turn in the stair. It brushed the wall with a dry rasp, an objection more persuasive than a committee. Marta called this a failed transport trial. I preferred an architectural delay. Anna drew the corridor beside my elegant design, and the issue ceased to be debatable without falsifying the scale. A detachable frame later passed, but no living vessel had been tested. I preserved that distinction when writing to the prospective patron.
prior_expectations: A scale-up plan would fit the tower
observations: A surrogate could not clear the corridor turn
decisions: I revised the detachable frame but withheld claims about living subjects
consequences: Scale-up retained an explicit transport limitation
belief_changes: A surrogate result is not evidence of organism viability
relationship_changes: Anna and Marta insisted upon honest scale boundaries
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: An Invoice with Two Names
memory_text: A printer sent a bill addressed to Julian and me jointly for illustrations I had commissioned. I had joined our names from tenderness, a motive which looked suspiciously like authorization once printed. Julian returned the invoice, agreeing to inspect the drawings but refusing to pay for work undertaken without his consent. I could hear rain striking the shutters while I read his answer. Marta said the objection was both clear and fair. I told her the pictures had been meant as a gift. She asked why a gift arrived with a debt. I paid the bill and admitted the mistake without decorating the apology. Julian replied concerning the paper quality, which was perhaps the kindest possible outcome.
prior_expectations: Joint credit would be understood as generosity
observations: Julian refused liability for an unapproved project
decisions: I paid and apologized
consequences: Our correspondence continued without that obligation
belief_changes: Affection does not confer authority over another's name
relationship_changes: Julian asserted a practical boundary
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Broken Song
memory_text: A damaged tooth in the music box interrupted the Ballerina's familiar phrase. She moved at the usual interval, then stopped. I preferred to call this disappointment. Clara reminded me that she sometimes moved before any note sounded. We played the broken fragment by hand and obtained another interval. The metallic click of the failing mechanism troubled me more than the spoiled music because our previous results were no longer easy to compare. I had Lenz retain the faulty tooth when he repaired the box. Too often I had polished away the reasons a later measurement differed from its predecessor. The damaged part went into an envelope with its date. In time the click reminded me less of failure than of the relief of knowing which instrument had produced it.
prior_expectations: The incomplete melody would reveal an artistic preference
observations: Crank behavior was a competing explanation
decisions: I kept the damaged component and recorded different timings
consequences: The tooth became a longitudinal cue for apparatus identity
belief_changes: Equipment histories matter to behavioral interpretation
relationship_changes: Clara's rival hypothesis remained in the ledger
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: What the Frame Omitted
memory_text: Julian showed me a portrait darkened by varnish. He had cleaned one strip and left the remaining work to the owner. I said the restoration was incomplete. He answered that an honest fragment was preferable to a handsome invention. The workshop smelled of beeswax and turpentine, odors I had long associated with competent hands. Julian invited me to look at a frame I had no wish to improve. I declined the bait. On the train home, the same resin odor lingered in my coat. It recalled his question before it recalled the portrait. That order displeased me. It was also evidence that my supposed hierarchy of interesting objects had been assigned by someone other than the doctor.
prior_expectations: Restoration should always complete the ideal
observations: Julian stopped where evidence ceased
decisions: I accepted the unfinished work without correction
consequences: The resin odor became an association with Julian's autonomy
belief_changes: Restraint can preserve fidelity
relationship_changes: Julian retained the independence of his craft
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Performance I Cancelled
memory_text: A visitor requested a demonstration of the Devil's famous defiance. The flattering description nearly persuaded me. Anna asked whether I intended to repeat the saucer performance the creature had already refused. I prepared the gallery anyway. That morning I heard him tapping within the enclosure; he stopped when voices reached the door. I could not prove that the voices caused his silence. I could prove that no exhibition was owed. I cancelled it, citing unsuitable conditions, a phrase which rescued a portion of my dignity. The visitor replied that science had grown sentimental. I kept the letter because the accusation was almost handsome enough to borrow.
prior_expectations: A flattering audience justified a repeated display
observations: The creature did not produce the requested behavior
decisions: I cancelled rather than compel it
consequences: Unpredictability became a constraint on demonstrations
belief_changes: A subject is not a performance contract
relationship_changes: Anna's objection changed my conduct
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: Two Notebooks at the Ledge
memory_text: Anna brought her observations to the Queen's ledge. Marta laid the blue ledger beside them. One notebook recorded what the inhabitant did; the other, why I believed she did it. An old entry called the Queen grateful for my new shelter. Anna asked which movement had distinguished gratitude from relief at being left alone. I could name none. I felt the warmth of the lamp across my hands and remembered Clara making me lower the curtain decades earlier. I did not erase the old sentence. I wrote a second interpretation beside it with a date. To conceal my earlier confidence would misrepresent how I arrived at later caution. Any successors might learn from my errors as well as my methods.
prior_expectations: Old interpretation would agree with later observation
observations: The inference of gratitude lacked an observable discriminator
decisions: I appended a dated alternate interpretation
consequences: Changing beliefs became part of the archive
belief_changes: Revision should not erase earlier mistakes
relationship_changes: Anna and Marta gained interpretive standing
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.

title: The Photograph Smelled of Vinegar
memory_text: An old photograph had faded along an edge. I carried it to the darkroom expecting to find a neglected chemical bath. The wet tray smelled of vinegar, and at once I remembered the cleaning cloth Marta had discovered behind the northern cabinet many years before. I was briefly certain that the same error had damaged the picture. Anna examined its backing and proposed light exposure instead. We stored the damaged print beside a fresh copy. That evening I thought I smelled vinegar while opening a dry envelope. I noted the possibility that I had anticipated the odor rather than encountered it. The doubt survived longer than the picture. In the archive both impressions remain available without requiring that either prove a cause.
prior_expectations: The familiar odor explained the fading
observations: Inspection favored light exposure and an anticipated odor remained uncertain
decisions: I preserved both photographs and recorded the uncertainty
consequences: Vinegar linked distinct settings without demonstrating a cause
belief_changes: Sensory familiarity is not chemical diagnosis
relationship_changes: Anna and Marta separated current evidence from remembered smell
alternative_interpretation: The narrator may be selective or misinfer another person's motivation.
